limitations: The rule does not test the equals argument, compare character contents, inspect a returned hash code, or observe whether the call returns normally.

Because AspectJ `call` matching uses the static type used to access a method, a call selected through a supertype such as Object can be outside this `CharSequence+` call-signature pattern even when the runtime receiver implements CharSequence.
The rule has no collection/map event, so it cannot establish that a warned value was actually used as a key or set element.
The rule does not evaluate whether a nonexcluded concrete implementation has separately documented compatible equality and hash-code behavior.
The rule gives no agent/weaver coverage guarantee for code that was not instrumented.
predicates: `before()` advice logs the warning before the selected call proceeds.
`CharSequence+` is an AspectJ subtype pattern, including CharSequence itself and its subtypes.
`target(T)` is runtime target-object matching; it is not a test of the identifier, cast, or source spelling used by the caller.
detector_semantics.claim: A matching call invokes an equals- or hashCode-named member through the CharSequence type family without one of the rule's two runtime target exclusions; therefore the detector reports that equality and hash-code support might not be suitable for arbitrary CharSequence use.

unknowns: The rule source does not identify the agent version, weaving mode, scope of instrumented classes, or whether all intended call sites are observable in a particular deployment.
The rule does not specify a particular Java release beyond linking to Java SE 6 documentation; concrete implementation behavior and compatibility must be checked for the runtime actually used.
The rule does not state why String and CharBuffer alone are excluded, nor does it enumerate other concrete CharSequence implementations that may provide safe, documented equality/hash-code semantics.
The rule does not establish whether a finding concerns Object.equals(Object)/Object.hashCode() or a same-named overload permitted by its wildcard signature patterns.
No per-finding evidence in this specification identifies the concrete runtime target class, compared operand, hash value, call outcome, or downstream data-structure use.

documented_behavior: The Java SE 6 documentation for `java.lang.CharSequence` states that the interface does not refine the general contracts of `equals` and `hashCode`; comparison between two CharSequence implementations is generally undefined, and arbitrary CharSequence instances are inappropriate as set elements or map keys.
`java.lang.Object` specifies the general `equals(Object)` equivalence-relation contract and the requirement that equal objects produce the same hash code.
`java.lang.String` defines equality against another String and specifies its hash-code computation.
`java.nio.CharBuffer` defines equality among char buffers and a content-dependent hash code.
preconditions: The documented CharSequence caution applies to arbitrary CharSequence implementations and does not by itself describe the behavior of a particular concrete implementation.
A concrete instance-method call requires a usable non-null receiver to reach the invoked implementation; a null receiver cannot demonstrate an implementation's equality/hash-code semantics.
CharBuffer documentation cautions that its content-dependent hash code makes it inadvisable to use a buffer as a hash-map key unless its contents will not change.
unknowns: Whether a particular nonexcluded concrete CharSequence class documents an equality domain and hash-code behavior suitable for its intended comparison or keying use.
Whether both operands, if any, have the same concrete implementation and whether that implementation deliberately supports the comparison.
Whether the selected method is the standard Object-signature method or an application-defined overload admitted by the broad `(..)` rule pattern.

events.condition: Before a method-call join point matching `call(* CharSequence+.equals(..))`, provided the runtime receiver does not match `target(String)` and does not match `target(CharBuffer)`. `CharSequence+` includes java.lang.CharSequence and its subtypes; `target(T)` evaluates the runtime target type, including matching subtypes, rather than the source identifier or cast. The `*` return-type and `(..)` argument-list patterns are unrestricted.
events.name: equals

events.condition: Before a method-call join point matching `call(* CharSequence+.hashCode(..))`, provided the runtime receiver does not match `target(String)` and does not match `target(CharBuffer)`. `CharSequence+` includes java.lang.CharSequence and its subtypes; `target(T)` evaluates the runtime target type, including matching subtypes, rather than the source identifier or cast. The `*` return-type and `(..)` argument-list patterns are unrestricted.
events.name: hashCode

important_note: This is a warning rule, not proof that an invoked method is absent, throws, violates Object's equals/hashCode contract, or causes a collection failure. Its concern is that java.lang.CharSequence itself does not refine cross-implementation equality or hash-code semantics. The rule warns before matching calls unless the runtime target is a String or CharBuffer, including a subtype matched by AspectJ `target(Type)`.
forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: That a warned target has no equals or hashCode method. Every object inherits those Object methods unless it overrides them.
That a warned concrete CharSequence implementation violates the Object.equals(Object) or Object.hashCode() contract.
That two particular CharSequence implementations compare incorrectly, asymmetrically, or with inconsistent hash codes.
That the call was used as a Set element, Map key, cache key, authorization decision, or other security-sensitive operation.
That the warning concerns only the exact source spelling `CharSequence`; the `CharSequence+` signature pattern includes matching subtypes, while exclusions are evaluated against the runtime target.
That the called equals or hashCode has the conventional Object signature only; the rule's `*` return-type and `(..)` parameter patterns also admit matching overloads declared on a matching subtype.
That String or CharBuffer targets trigger this rule; the rule expressly excludes runtime targets matching those types.

security_semantics.runtime_claim: A finding establishes only that an instrumented matching call event occurred before the call, with a runtime target that did not match the String or CharBuffer exclusions.
security_semantics.detector_claim: The detector reports a potential API-contract ambiguity involving equality or hash-code calls on nonexcluded CharSequence-family targets.

compatibility: Confirm the Java runtime/library version and the concrete CharSequence implementation version whose contract is being relied upon.
Confirm the deployed AspectJ/RV-Monitor agent or weaving configuration preserves the rule's call-join-point and runtime-target semantics.
Do not infer a universal cross-type equality policy from the CharSequence interface; compatibility must be established for the concrete implementation pair.
runtime: Show that the matching call executes in code covered by the monitor/weaver.
Show the runtime receiver class at the call; the event predicate is satisfied only when it is not a String or CharBuffer target under AspectJ target-type matching.
For a behavioral defect claim, record the equality results and hash values for the relevant concrete instances and execution state.
source_level: Establish that the selected call signature is accessed through java.lang.CharSequence or a subtype, as required by `call(* CharSequence+.<method>(..))`.
Identify the actual concrete target class and inspect its authoritative API documentation or source for equals(Object), hashCode(), and any relevant overloads.
If the concern is collection behavior, show the separate source-level flow placing the value in a Set, Map, cache, or equivalent hash-based structure.

name: CharSequence_UndefinedHashCode
semantic_scope: For every finding of this rule, the detector observes a method-call join point before a call whose method signature has a static access/declaring type matching java.lang.CharSequence or a subtype and whose name is equals or hashCode, with any return type and any argument list. It emits the warning only when the runtime receiver is neither a java.lang.String nor a java.nio.CharBuffer, including their AspectJ-matched subtypes. It observes the call before completion, not the return value, exception, equality result, hash value, concrete implementation's documentation, or downstream use of the result.
known_false_positive_shapes: A nonexcluded concrete CharSequence implementation has its own documented, contract-compliant equals(Object) and hashCode() behavior, but the rule warns because it does not inspect that implementation's contract.
The call compares an object only with itself or with the same known concrete implementation; the rule does not inspect the argument or establish cross-implementation comparison.
The call result is unused or otherwise has no hash-based collection consequence; the rule warns on the call itself.

A call receiver evaluates to null: it does not match the String or CharBuffer target exclusions, and the before-call advice can warn even though the subsequent invocation cannot assess a concrete CharSequence implementation.

A matching subtype declares an overload named equals or hashCode with a nonstandard parameter list or return type; the pointcut's `(..)` and `*` patterns are broader than the conventional Object methods.
protocol: (before equals) | (before hashCode); each event is independent and has no required predecessor or successor
